title: ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.setConnectTimeout throws 'Timeout must be a non-negative value' for very long timeouts: cap at Integer.MAX_VALUE seconds
errorSample:
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Timeout must be a non-negative value
	at org.springframework.util.Assert.isTrue(Assert.java:117) ~[spring-core-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.http.client.ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.setConnectTimeout(ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.java:156) ~[spring-web-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.http.client.ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.setConnectTimeout(ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.java:169) ~[spring-web-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at task.PartnerApiConfig.partnerRestClient(Application.kt:30) ~[main/:na]
symptom: Building a RestClient on ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory fails with IllegalArgumentException: Timeout must be a non-negative value when the configured connect timeout is 30 days; 7 days works.
cause: The factory stores timeouts as a 32-bit integer number of seconds, so a Duration above Integer.MAX_VALUE seconds is narrowed to a negative value and fails the non-negative assertion.
fixSummary: Cap the configured Duration to the largest supported value before calling the setter: requestFactory.setConnectTimeout(minOf(properties.connectTimeout, Duration.ofSeconds(Int.MAX_VALUE.toLong()))). The configured 30d stays as the intent and larger values are limited instead of overflowing.
